item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 290206
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM EDT Mon Sep 28 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Fay, located well to the west-southwest of the Azores,
and on Tropical Storm Hanna, located well to the east-northeast of
Bermuda.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected over the next 7 days.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Hanna are issued under WMO
header WTNT33 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT3.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Hanna are issued under WMO
header WTNT23 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT3.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

...FAY REACHES TROPICAL STORM STRENGTH AGAIN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM AST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...26.0N 45.9W
ABOUT 1380 MI...2215 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...SW OR 230 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1008 MB...29.77 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM AST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was 
located near latitude 26.0 North, longitude 45.9 West. Fay is moving 
toward the southwest near 10 mph (17 km/h). A southwest to 
west-southwest motion, along with an increase in forward speed, is 
expected to continue over the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 40 mph (65 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Little change in strength is forecast during the next 
day or so, and Fay is forecast to become a post-tropical cyclone in 
36 h.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1008 mb (29.77 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM AST.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Hagen

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 35
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM AST Mon Sep 28 2026 
861 
WTNT41 KNHC 282032
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  35
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
500 PM AST Mon Sep 28 2026
 
Fay has continued to produce bursts of deep convection this 
afternoon, primarily sheared to the south of the low-level center. 
The overall satellite presentation has improved slightly since 
earlier today, featuring cold cloud tops near -70C. Objective 
UW-CIMSS satellite intensity estimates have been running slightly 
higher than the scatterometer-derived surface wind data from earlier 
today. However, the subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB 
has held steady at T2.0/30 kt. Accordingly, the initial intensity is 
maintained at 30 kt for this advisory.
 
The depression is moving southwestward with an estimated initial 
motion of 220/8 kt. A general southwest to west-southwest motion is 
anticipated over the next couple of days as Fay is steered by the 
flow along the southern periphery of a mid-level ridge situated over 
the central Atlantic. The latest NHC track forecast is essentially 
an update of the previous advisory and lies very close to the HCCA 
corrected-consensus aid.
 
Fay continues to defy model guidance by maintaining deep convection 
near its low-level center. Given that vertical wind shear remains 
low-to-moderate and sea surface temperatures are near 29C, it is 
entirely possible that Fay could briefly regain tropical storm 
strength tonight. Global models persist in showing that the system 
will struggle to sustain deep convection in a day or so as it 
encounters a more stable air mass and upper-level convergence. 
Nevertheless, Fay has proven to be a resilient, small system. The 
latest NHC intensity forecast holds Fay steady through Tuesday 
followed by gradual weakening, with the system forecast to become a 
post-tropical cyclone in a day or so, and degenerate into a remnant 
trough in a couple of days.

item.title: Tropical Storm Hanna Forecast Discussion Number 2
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM AST Mon Sep 28 2026 
000
WTNT43 KNHC 282043
TCDAT3
 
Tropical Storm Hanna Discussion Number   2
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL082026
500 PM AST Mon Sep 28 2026
 
Since this morning, Hanna's convective structure has become a little 
more disheveled with the tropical storm is affected by 20-25 kt of 
westerly vertical wind shear. There has not been an appreciable 
change in the subjective or objective intensity estimates this 
afternoon, and the initial intensity is held at 40 kt.

The initial motion of Hanna is east-southeastward at 115 degrees at 
15 kt. Hanna is embedded in the flow in between a longwave trough to 
its northeast, and a larger subtropical ridge to its south. This 
synoptic pattern should result in a continued east-southeastward 
motion over the next 24-36 hours with some gradually slow down in 
the track as the mid-latitude trough leaves Hanna behind. Much of 
the track guidance then shows a slow east-northeastward motion 
after the cyclone becomes more vertically shallow and becomes 
influenced by a low-level ridge centered south of the Azores. The 
NHC track forecast is very similar to the previous one, roughly in 
between the simple (TVCN) and corrected consensus (HCCA) aids.

Vertical wind shear over Hanna is expected to persist in over the 
next 48-72 h, though because the tropical storm is currently moving 
in the same direction as the shear vector, bursts of deep convection 
down-shear of the center may allow for some slight intensification, 
which is reflected in the HCCA intensity guidance. However, when 
Hanna slows down and turned more east-northeastward, the shear is 
expected to shift more out of the north, importing very dry 
tropospheric air into the circulation. Simulated satellite imagery 
from the ECMWF and hurricane-regional models still show convection 
ceasing over the storm in around 60 h, marking its transition to a 
post-tropical cyclone in the forecast.
